title: Stream aggregator: KV-aware batch selection and GPU footprint compaction
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement a stream-aggregator heuristic for continuous batching that reduces per-request KV duplication and total GPU memory footprint for streaming chat completions. The goal is to merge compatible streaming requests into a single GPU allocation where safe, prioritize low-latency paths for interactive users, and fall back gracefully when KV prefix conflicts or memory constraints occur. Deliverables: algorithm spec, cost model, prototype implementation, benchmark results, rollout plan with feature flags and canary.
comments: 2026-02-11 - Triage: Identified repeated problem where multiple concurrent chat sessions with similar prefixes were allocating distinct KV slots, inflating GPU resident memory. Decided to explore prefix-merge + slot compaction approach rather than purely increasing slab sizes.

2026-02-18 - Design spike: Implemented a prototype stream-aggregator that groups in-flight streams by (model, quantization, prefix-hash, max-allowed-latency). Added 'frame' abstraction that bundles compatible KV prefixes into a shared allocation and maintains reference counts to enable safe eviction.

2026-02-24 - Experiment: Ran a 24h A/B on a synthetic chat workload (mix: 60% short Q/A, 30% mid conversations, 10% long context). Results: mean GPU memory per worker down 18%, KV cache hit rate up from 62% to 79%, overall tokens/sec +12%. P95 tail latency for interactive flows increased +4ms (within SLO).

2026-03-01 - Review: PM (Lina Gomez) asked for clarity on customer impact when prefix mismatches occur. Decided to add a fast-path 'no-merge' policy for sessions marked real-time and allow non-critical sessions to be merged aggressively.

2026-03-04 - Security/Compliance note: No new exfiltration risk observed; aggregator only merges identical prefixes and keeps per-session attribution in metadata. Security review requested later in rollout for enterprise-private deployments.

2026-03-07 - Engineering feedback: Rajiv suggested tracking per-frame fragmentation metric and a compaction pass that runs during low-util windows to re-pack sparsely used frames. Recorded as follow-up task ENG-31877.

2026-03-09 - Implementation: Core allocator changes pushed in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1984. Added unit tests and a microbenchmark harness. Integration tests show no correctness regressions for KV lookups.

2026-03-12 - Next steps: Add feature flag (stream_aggregator_v1) with three modes: disabled, safe-merge, aggressive-merge. Plan a staged canary on dedicated pools for runtime-1.21 release. Instrument console dashboards with new metrics: frame_count, frame_fragmentation, merged_sessions, merge_fail_reasons.
